name: Credit Karma
description: Intuit Credit Karma provides consumer credit reports and scores, credit and identity monitoring, financial tracking, personalized financial-product offers, dispute tools, and tax-filing access.
agentUseSummary: Credit Karma cannot currently be connected as an autonomous Relay provider. Its official member experience is an interactive, identity-bound consumer service, while Intuit's documented financial-data interfaces are partner ingestion channels for contracted financial institutions rather than a public member-account API. Credit Karma does not publish a Relay-usable remote MCP endpoint, member OAuth scopes, stable tool schemas, service credentials, or revocation contract. Relay will not reuse sessions, capture credentials, retrieve consumer reports, or automate disputes, applications, tax filing, or money movement.

blocked.label: Connect Credit Karma through an unsupported session
blocked.description: Relay will not reuse a Credit Karma or Intuit browser session, capture member credentials or tokens, automate identity verification or consent, or reinterpret a contracted financial-institution feed as member-account authority.

blocked.label: Access private credit, identity, or financial data
blocked.description: Credit reports, scores, factors, inquiries, accounts, balances, payments, addresses, Social Security numbers, breach alerts, linked institutions, transactions, cash flow, net worth, tax information, and personalized offers are blocked without a supported least-privilege member API contract.

blocked.label: Act on credit reports or financial offers
blocked.description: Credit-report disputes, credit locks or freezes, monitoring changes, recommendations, prequalification, Approval Odds, loan or card applications, insurance actions, and disclosure of consumer-report information are blocked.

blocked.label: File taxes or move money
blocked.description: TurboTax account linking, tax-document sharing, return preparation or filing, refund routing, bank-account changes, Credit Karma Money actions, transfers, withdrawals, deposits, Credit Builder actions, and every other consequential financial action are blocked.

blocked.label: Use unsupported Credit Karma automation
blocked.description: Dashboard scraping, private endpoint discovery, UI automation, raw session pass-through, account impersonation, and use of consumer information under false pretenses are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No Credit Karma action can be enabled without a supported public member authorization and tool contract designed for third-party autonomous use.

runtimeSupport.description: Credit Karma publishes no member-account API/MCP authorization or bounded tool contract that Relay can distribute as OpenClaw tools.
Credit Karma publishes no member-account API/MCP authorization or bounded tool contract that Relay can distribute as Hermes tools.

providerSetup.blocker: Credit Karma is an identity-bound consumer financial service handling credit reports, scores, government identifiers, linked financial accounts, transactions, personalized offers, disputes, tax access, and money features. Intuit documents contracted financial-institution data-ingestion standards, but no public Relay-usable member API/MCP endpoint, stable tool schemas, member OAuth scopes, service credentials, revocation lifecycle, or third-party autonomous authorization boundary.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not expose Connect, request Credit Karma credentials, reuse a member session, scrape the dashboard, retrieve consumer reports, automate disputes or applications, link TurboTax, or move money. Reconsider only if Credit Karma publishes a supported third-party member API or remote MCP contract with versioned schemas, least-privilege scopes, revocation, exact consumer binding, FCRA-compliant permissible-purpose controls, audit semantics, data-retention controls, and explicit confirmation for every dispute, application, tax, credit-lock, account-linking, or money action.

evidence.supports: Credit Karma documents identity-bound access to Equifax and TransUnion credit reports and scores, daily monitoring, Approval Odds, cash-flow and net-worth tracking, identity monitoring, Direct Dispute, personalized financial-product offers, and TurboTax-powered filing inside the consumer app.

Credit Karma's current terms require each member to register only for themselves, prohibit sharing account access, require a valid U.S. Social Security number, describe consent to retrieve consumer reports and other personal data, prohibit obtaining consumer information under false pretenses, and prohibit reverse engineering.

Intuit's documented Financial Data Platform interfaces are implementation resources for organizations that provide financial transaction data to Intuit products using standards such as OAuth 2, OpenID Connect, FAPI, FDX, Open Banking, and OFX; they do not publish a Credit Karma member-account API or autonomous consumer authorization contract.

Intuit identifies Credit Karma support through managed aggregation and describes Web Connect or Direct Connect as contracted financial-institution connectivity, confirming that these partner feeds are not public member-account access for third-party agents.
